(p-٣69)In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Sūrat al-Qiyāmah (The Resurrection).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾ ﴿and I swear by the reproaching soul﴾

Ibn Jarīr said: The reciters differed in the recitation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read ﴿lā uqsimu﴾ with "lā" separated from "uqsimu", except al-Ḥasan and al-A'raj, for it is reported from them that they used to recite it as ﴿la-uqsimu bi-yawmi al-qiyāmah﴾, meaning: "I swear by the Day of Resurrection."

Then the lām of oath (lām al-qasam) entered upon it. The recitation which I do not permit other than in this place is "lā" separated, and "uqsimu" beginning a new clause, as the majority of the reciters of the cities read it, by the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

Those who read it in the manner we have chosen have differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: "lā" is superfluous (ṣilah), and the meaning of the speech is: "I swear by the Day of Resurrection," and he attributed this to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.

Others said: Rather, "lā" entered for emphasis of the speech.

It is reported from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh regarding His saying ﴿lā uqsimu﴾ that it is an emphasis of the oath, like the saying: "lā wallāhi" (no, by Allah).

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: "lā" is a rejection of a statement that preceded from the speech of the polytheists who used to deny Paradise and Hell.

Then the oath began, so it was said: ﴿uqsimu bi-yawmi al-qiyāmah﴾. He (the grammarian) used to say: every oath preceded by a statement is a rejection, so it is necessary to place "lā" before it, in order to distinguish thereby between the oath which is a denial and the oath which is newly begun. He said: Do you not see that you say, beginning: "By Allah, the Messenger is true," and when you say: "No, by Allah, the Messenger is true," it is as if you have refuted a people who denied it? They also differed regarding this, whether it is an oath or not.

He mentioned the disagreement on that. The reality is that this question is among the difficult ones, from the standpoint of the presence of the lām: is it negating the oath or affirming it? And if it is affirming, what does it imply? Is it a rejection of a previous statement or an emphasis of the oath? Did an oath actually occur or not? All of this was mentioned by Ibn Jarīr.

(p-370) The Shaykh—may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him—addressed it in his book Daf' Īhām al-Iḍṭirāb (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction) in two places. The first: in this sūrah. The second: in Sūrat al-Balad at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿lā uqsimu bi-hādhā al-balad﴾ [al-Balad: 1]. In the first place he clarified that it—i.e., "lā"—is a negation of a statement before it; so it does not conflict with the oath by the Day of Resurrection, the verb of which occurs in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿wa-al-yawmi al-mawʿūd﴾ [al-Burūj: 2].

The second: that it is superfluous (ṣilah). He said: further clarification of it will come. The second place is ﴿lā uqsimu bi-hādhā al-balad﴾, in which he presented a very long and extremely important discussion, whose summary we shall set out. The book will be printed, God willing, with this supplement, so let it be referred to.

The summary of what he presented, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him:

He said: The answer to it is from several aspects. The first—and the majority hold it—is that "lā" here is superfluous (ṣilah) according to the custom of the Arabs, for they sometimes utter the word "lā" without intending its original meaning, but merely to strengthen and emphasize the speech, like His saying: ﴿What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me?﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 92–93]. That is, "an tattabiʿanī" (that you follow me).

And His saying: ﴿so that the People of the Scripture may know﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29].

And His saying: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they do not believe﴾ [al-Nisā': 65].

And the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

﴿So no, by your father, daughter of al-ʿĀmirī, the people will not claim that I flee﴾

That is, "wa-abīki" (and by your father). He cited, al-Farrāʾ, for the superfluity of "lā" in speech that carries the sense of denial, the verse of the poet:

"The Messenger of Allah did not approve their religion, / and the two best men, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar"

That is, "wa-ʿUmar" (and ʿUmar). Al-Jawharī cited for its superfluity the verse of al-ʿAjjāj:

"In a well of destruction, he travelled and was not aware / of his falsehood, until he saw the morning reveal (the trees)"

And al-ḥawr means destruction: that is, in a well of destruction. And another cited:

"I remembered Layla, and passionate longing overcame me, / and the core of my heart almost, without ceasing, was cut off"

The second aspect: "lā" is a negation of the statement of the polytheists who denied the Prophet ﷺ.

(p-371) His saying "uqsimu" is an affirmation newly begun.

It was said: this aspect, though many scholars held it, is not sound in my view, because of His saying, exalted is He, in Sūrat al-Qiyāmah: ﴿and I swear by the reproaching soul﴾; for His saying ﴿and I swear by the reproaching soul﴾ indicates that He did not intend a newly begun affirmation after the negation with His saying "uqsimu". And Allah knows best.

The third aspect: it is also a particle of negation, and its basis is that the act of making an oath implicitly contains information about the magnification of the one sworn by. So it is a negation of that implicit statement by way of kināyah (indirect expression). What is meant is that He is not magnified by the oath; rather He is great in Himself, whether He is sworn by or not. This view was mentioned by the author of al-Kashshāf and the author of Rūḥ al-Maʿānī, and in my view it is not free from scrutiny.

The fourth aspect: the lām is the lām of initiation (lām al-ibtidāʾ), its fatḥah lengthened. The Arabs sometimes lengthen the fatḥah into an alif, the kasrah into a yāʾ, and the ḍammah into a wāw. An example of the fatḥah is the saying of ʿAbd Yaghūth ibn al-Ḥārith:

"And a Shaykhah of ʿAbd Shams laughs at me, / as if she had not seen before me a Yemeni captive"

The original is "ka-an lam tara," but the fatḥah was lengthened.

And the saying of the rājiz:

"When the old woman becomes angry, divorce her, / and do not appease her nor flatter her"

And the saying of ʿAntarah in his Muʿallaqah:

"It flows from the nape of a furious, swift she-camel, / quick-paced, like a well-polished ancient one"

The original is "yanbaʿu" (it flows), meaning the sweat flows from the nape: from his she-camel; so the fatḥah was lengthened and it became "yanbāʿu." He said: this lengthening is not out of necessity of poetry.

Then he cited the evidences for lengthening with ḍammah and kasrah. Then he said: this aspect is supported by the recitation of Qunbul: ﴿la-uqsimu bi-hādhā al-balad﴾ with the lām of initiation, and it is transmitted from al-Bazzī and al-Ḥasan. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He. End, summarized.

So you see that he (may Allah have mercy on him) presented four aspects: superfluity (ṣilah), negation of the statement before it, emphasis of the oath, and the lām of initiation. He cited as evidence for it the recitation of Qunbul, namely "la-uqsimu" joined. As for its being a lām of initiation by the recitation of Qunbul and al-Ḥasan, it has already been mentioned that Ibn Jarīr does not permit this recitation, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on reading it separated: ﴿lā uqsimu﴾.

Perhaps the most preferred of all these aspects is that it is for emphasis of the oath, as Ibn Jarīr mentioned from the grammarians of Kufa. And Allah knows best.

The author said in (Daf' Īhām al-Iḍṭirāb ʿan Āyāt al-Kitāb):

Sūrat al-Qiyāmah

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾.

It does not conflict with His swearing by it in His saying: ﴿and by the promised Day﴾ [85], and the answer is from two aspects:

One of them: that "lā" is a negation of the statement of the disbelievers.

The second: that it is superfluous (ṣilah), as has preceded, and further clarification of it will come, God willing, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 3:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?﴾

This assumption has been stated explicitly in the words of the Most High: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78].

And the answer to it came: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Yes, [We are] able to put together even his fingertips﴾.

All the exegetes agree that the meaning is: We would make his fingertips even and joined together like the sole of a camel (khuff al-ba'ir), that is, he would be unable to grasp anything with them or to perform any skilled work with them.

In reality, we do not understand a meaning for this in light of the context, although it does indicate the power of God and the helplessness of the servant. However, the context, with its denial and rejection of the resurrection, and the occurrence of a parallel to this in surah Ya-Sin, guides us to the understanding that He, glory be to Him, is able, after the death of the servant, his dissolution into dust, and the transformation of his bones into decayed remains, to restore him completely, just as He originated him the first time. Included in that restoration is that He would put together his fingertips, that is, make them even and bring them into being as they were the first time. And God knows best.

Its guidance is found in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He is Knowing of every creation﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79]. Among creation is the form in which this denying, contrary human being was created, so He, glory be to Him, restores him exactly as he was. This is more eloquent in demonstrating power and more emphatic in establishing the proof on the Day of Resurrection. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when the sight is dazzled﴾ ﴿and the moon is eclipsed﴾ ﴿and the sun and moon are joined together﴾ ﴿On that Day man will say, "Where is the escape?"﴾ ﴿No! There is no refuge!﴾

"Bariqa" (بَرِقَ) has been recited with a kasra on the ra' and with a fatha on the ra'. With the kasra, it means he was frightened and bewildered. Its origin is from "baraqa al-rajul," when a man looked at the lightning and his sight was dazzled. From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"Had Luqman the wise been confronted, with Mayy unveiled before his eyes, he would nearly have been dazzled."

And the saying of al-A'sha:

"I used to see in the face of Mayyah a glimpse, and I would be dazzled, my place overcome with fainting."

And "baraqa" with a fatha means his sight was split (or fixed in a stare), and it comes from "al-bareeq" (glitter), meaning his sight shone from the intensity of its staring.

Abu Hayyan said: The reality is that there is no obstacle to intending both meanings, since both recitations are sound. This text may also be supported by His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Ibrahim: ﴿He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ ﴿hastening forward, with their heads raised, their glance not returning to them﴾ [Ibrahim: 42-43].

Ibn Kathir said: They look out of terror this way and that, and no gaze settles on them from the intensity of the dread.

As for His saying: ﴿On that Day man will say, "Where is the escape?"﴾ ﴿No! There is no refuge!﴾, it has already been mentioned to the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, in Surah Sad at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How many generations before them did We destroy, and they cried out when there was no longer any time for escape﴾ [Sad: 3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 13:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾

The meaning of "what he sent ahead" (bi-ma qaddama) here is the deeds he sent ahead for the Day of Resurrection, as in His statement, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him?﴾ ﴿He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead for my life"﴾ [al-Fajr: 23-24]. The explanation of this was preceded by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) at His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned﴾ [al-Zumar: 48], in the surah of "al-Zumar".

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, man will be a witness against himself﴾

It is explained by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Read your record. Your own soul suffices against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 14].

And His saying: ﴿And they will find whatever they did present there﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], and it has preceded in surah "al-Kahf."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Even if he were to offer his excuses﴾

That is: their excuses will not benefit them at that time, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day when their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong﴾ [Ghafir: 52].

(p-374) And Allah, exalted is He, has explained some of those excuses in such verses as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those against whom the Word has been justified will say: "Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray; we led them astray just as we ourselves went astray. We disavow to You; it was not us they worshipped"﴾ [al-Qasas: 63].

And His saying: ﴿So we led you astray, for we ourselves were astray﴾ [al-Saffat: 32].

And His saying: ﴿They will say: "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people. Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return, we will indeed be wrongdoers." He will say: "Remain in it in disgrace, and do not speak to Me."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 106–108].

And His saying: ﴿And they will say: "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze." So they will acknowledge their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 10–11].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾

In it is the prohibition against moving his tongue (ﷺ), and the clarification that Allah, exalted is He, has taken upon Himself its collection and its recitation. This indicates that he (ﷺ), out of his intense eagerness to retain what was revealed to him, would move his tongue at the time of revelation (wahy, divine inspiration), so he was forbidden from doing that.

Allah, exalted is He, has made clear the extent of this prohibition and the duration of this haste in His saying: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 114]. In it is also an allusion to the good of listening and attentiveness at the time of its being revealed, as in the etiquette of listening: ﴿So listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 204].

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 17], Allah, exalted is He, has clarified that its collection and its recitation upon him is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9].

Note (tanbih).

In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾ there is an indication that it was revealed in parts (mufarraqan), and an indication that its collection in this form that exists is by the care and attention of Allah, exalted is He, and its verification. The evidence for this is that this collection which exists is among the means of its preservation, as Allah, exalted is He, has guaranteed. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

And Abu Hayyan said: ﴿Upon Us is its collection﴾ in your breast. "And its recitation" means: you recite it.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿So when We have recited it, follow its recitation﴾.

The shaykh's explanation of this has already preceded, at His saying: ﴿He has been taught by one mighty in power﴾ [an-Najm: 5], in Surah "an-Najm" (The Star).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed upon Us is its explanation﴾

Exalted is He has drawn attention, as is stated in the introduction to Adwa' al-Bayan, that there is no mujmal (general, unspecified statement) except that its tafsil (detailed explanation) has come in another place. Exalted is He has expressly stated this in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been detailed﴾ [Fussilat: 3]. The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained this at the beginning of Surat Fussilat.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 22:

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾

Its explanation has already been given by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, at the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You." He said: "You will not see Me."﴾ [al-A'raf: 143].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾ ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾.

The way of reconciling this with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Vision does not comprehend Him﴾ [al-An'am: 103] has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay! When it reaches the collarbones﴾ ﴿and it is said, "Who can cure him?"﴾ ﴿and he realises that it is the parting﴾ ﴿and leg is entwined with leg﴾ ﴿to your Lord, that Day, is the driving﴾.

He did not specify what it is that reaches the collarbones, but it is known that it is the soul (ruh), as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why then, when it reaches the throat, and you are at that time looking on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see, will you not, if you are not under authority, bring it back, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83–87]. These are the states of death-agony (nazc), and the soul reaches the throat and reaches the collarbones. The explicit mention may be omitted for the sake of knowledge, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, I have loved the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord until it [the sun] disappeared behind the veil﴾ [Sad: 32], meaning the sun. Likewise here, since it is known from the context, He omitted explicit mention of the soul or the self (nafs). He, may He be exalted, has indeed stated this explicitly in His saying: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming pangs of death, and the angels are extending their hands, [saying], "Bring out your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation"...﴾ [al-An'am: 93], to the end of the verse.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and it is said, "Who can cure him?"﴾

Scholars differed over the meaning of "rāq" (who can cure/raise) here. It was said that it derives from ruqyah (incantation/healing), meaning: those around him said, "Who will treat him? Is there a physician who will cure him?" — that is, when the matter becomes severe upon him, hoping for his recovery, or deeming it unlikely that anyone can benefit him. And it was said: it derives from ruqiy (ascent), meaning the angels say: "Who is it that will ascend with his soul — the angels of punishment or the angels of mercy?"

However, the verse contains an indicator that the first is more preferred, because the statement of the angels occurs regarding a person who is hesitant about his matter, and this is not a place of hesitation here, since the context ends with: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed﴾ ﴿but rather denied and turned away﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 31–32], and what follows it.

Abu Hayyan said: "Even if it is according to the statement of the angels, 'Who will ascend with him [his soul]?', this would be out of their aversion to ascending with it." In this there is scrutiny, because Allah, may He be exalted, appointed angels for the polytheists, who are the angels of punishment, and angels for the believers, who are the angels of mercy. Neither group would be averse to ascending with what they are specifically assigned to, rather one of them may not even permit the other to take what is its own.

As in the hadith of the one who killed a hundred souls, and death overtook him halfway along the road; the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment came to him disputing which of them would ascend with his soul. Each wanted to take charge of seizing his soul. Those said: "He killed a hundred souls and never did a good deed at all," and those said: "He came out repentant to Allah, may He be exalted."

This is as has preceded from the Shaykh — may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him — regarding preferring one of the two meanings disputed among the exegetes, due to the presence of an indicator in the verse. The indicator has been found, namely what is at the end of the verse and the context, that it is not a place of hesitation: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 31], the verse. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾

This is a refutation of the claim that he was created neglected and aimless, and that he will not be called to account or questioned, and consequently will not be resurrected.

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) had already explained this at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ ﴿So exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115-116], meaning: Allah is exalted above purposelessness (ʿabath). The Shaykh presented the comprehensive proofs there.

(p-377) "Did he not used to be a sperm-drop emitted (in ejaculation)? Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned him. And He made of him two mates, the male and the female. Is not He able to give life to the dead?" Yes, He is able to do all things. The coming of this interrogative, which is either denunciatory or affirmative, after "Does man think that he will be left neglected?" and the recitation of these magnificent verses that point to His overwhelming power, contains a refutation of an implicit denial, namely that he does not believe in his being left neglected, nor in a reckoning for him, except for one who considers resurrection far-fetched.

Had he acknowledged the resurrection, he would have believed in recompense, admitted accountability, known that he was not created in vain, and that he would not be left neglected. But when he denied the resurrection, he supposed and reckoned that he would be left neglected. So the reminder of him of the origin of his creation and his development came in order to draw from him an acknowledgment, because whoever was able to create him from an emitted sperm-drop, and to develop him into a clot and then into a well-formed creature, is able to resurrect him once more.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has explained these stages in more than one place, and referred to them at His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted, and that upon Him is the second creation﴾ [al-Najm: 45–47], in Surat "al-Najm."
